text:
I just wasn't going to spend €820 for a "bare-bones" 4070 Ti, even though that's the card I actually wanted. The 4070 Gaming OC looked like a nice "semi-sensible downgrade"-option, although I usually don't go for these overbuilt coolers sitting on a middle of the road GPU. That said: I got the card for just €30 over what the cheapest 4070s would've cost (flash-sale) and I've been happy with my decision. The card will easily OC to nearly 3000 MHz and I also run it with an added 1000 MHz on the VRAM in Afterburner. Even with those settings, hotspot temps will only hit low 80°Cs while benchmarking - the card runs much cooler in games. Max power-limit is insanely high and can be set to 148% (around 300W if baseline is the 200W of the reference board). In the real world and with my OC, the card will draw just over 240W, even with power limit set to max. So... 300W is more of a "these go up to 11"-type of deal, but the card does allow higher power draw than the reference board.
On top of that: I really like the look of the card and it is very well built and feels solid. It is quite heavy (1.3, 1.4kg, IIRC) but it sits in my system without any sag. I probably wouldn't transport the PC with the card installed, though.

From my research into what manufacturer to go with: Do not buy the lower end MSI cards (Ventus line, basically). You'll pay more than for other brands, but the cooler MSI use on these isn't very well designed from what I found. It doesn't cover/touch all the VRMs for example and, IIRC, doesn't even allow airflow to those components. And that's true for both the 2 and 3 fan versions of the Ventus.

text: I have found the RTX 4070 is really good for 3D rendering in programs like Brice, Daz studio, and the IRAY render engine, (it also rendered really fast on 3D Studio Max, but i only had an upgrade trial copy because my licensed copy of 3DS Max is a decade old and is only used for modeling).   My personal benchmark was of a scene I created specifically to punish the GPU's. I rendered the same scene in Daz Studio using the IRAY engine at 4k resolution with 4k textures on every object set for a total of 3500 iterations.   My result for the 3 cards i have were the NVIDIA 2070 Super render time 6 hours and 43 min.   The RTX 3070 was 3 hours and 22 min , and the RTX 4070 cut it down to 44 min total!!!   (I was shocked as to how fast the 4070 rendered the scene)   I made no changes to the file before rendering, so all three cards were rendering the exact scene with zero changes.   I know this was not a formal bench test, but i thought I would share the results for the 3D modelers out there since most card reviews focus on games vs 3D programs.   Hope the info helps the modelers out there in the market for an upgrade.
